Total assets grew to EUR 2.597 billion with equity at EUR 1.175 billion.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key Figures of 2025 section, Management Report Overview

candidate_sentences.text: Aktsiaselts Infortar reported strong operational growth for the 2025 financial year, with consolidated revenue rising 33.9 percent to EUR 1,837 million compared to EUR 1,372 million in 2024.
EBITDA increased by 56.9 percent to EUR 227.9 million, expanding the EBITDA margin to 12.4 percent from 10.6 percent in the prior year.
Despite these top-line and operating improvements, net profit attributable to parent company owners declined by 63.1 percent to EUR 70.6 million from EUR 191.3 million in 2024.
Financial position strengthened further, with total equity rising slightly to EUR 1,175 million and the equity ratio improving to 45 percent from 43 percent.

Interest-bearing liabilities relative to equity decreased from 104.9 percent to 91 percent, while the net debt to EBITDA ratio improved from 4.0 to 3.7, reflecting active loan repayments and disciplined capital management.

verified_key_information_units.information: The revenue and EBITDA growth was primarily driven by the full-year consolidation of Tallink Grupp (acquired in August 2024), improved performance at Elenger Grupp, and contributions from newly consolidated agriculture assets including Estonia Farmid and Halinga.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Key Figures of 2025 commentary, Events in 2025 (Tallink, Energy, Agriculture sections)

candidate_sentences.text: The substantial growth in revenue and EBITDA is directly explained by the full twelve-month consolidation of Tallink Grupp, whereas its results were only partially consolidated from August onwards in 2024.
Additionally, the Elenger energy segment contributed an approximate EUR 12 million increase in EBITDA, supported by expanded infrastructure operations and new acquisitions in Poland and Latvia.
Infortar consolidated results also benefited from the inclusion of agriculture operations through the acquisition of Estonia Farmid and Halinga in 2025.

verified_key_information_units.information: The maritime transport segment carried 5.53 million passengers (0.9% decrease YoY), with cargo units down 19.2% to 245,004 and passenger vehicles down 2.2% to 760,473. Vessel chartering balanced seasonal revenue fluctuations, and technical upgrades focused on reducing CO₂ emissions.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Events in 2025 - Maritime transport business segment

verified_key_information_units.information: The energy segment delivered 18 TWh of LNG to Inkoo and Klaipėda terminals (unchanged YoY) with a market share of approximately 25% in the Finnish-Baltic region. Investments included a new 4.9 MW solar plant in Latvia and an 8 MWh battery storage facility, with plans for additional storage in Estonia.
verified_key_information_units.source_evidence: Events in 2025 - Energy business segment, Management Report Overview

verified_key_information_units.information: Real estate developments included completion of the 25,000 m² Rimi logistics centre in Laagri and commencement of construction for a 30,000 m² Depo DIY retail space in Lasnamäe. INF Infra secured a EUR 67.2 million contract for Rail Baltica mainline construction on the Kangru-Saku section.
Infortar acquired Estonia Farmid OÜ, gaining control of a major dairy farming and cereals operation, expanding its agriculture segment with the transaction completed on 7 July 2025.

details.completeness_justification: K1, K2, K6, K7, and K8 are fully represented with supporting sentences. K3 and K4 are entirely missing, as there is no mention of maritime transport passenger/cargo statistics or energy segment LNG volumes and investments. K5 is also missing, with no reference to real estate developments or Rail Baltica contracts. While financial metrics and strategic themes are well-covered, the absence of three HIGH-importance operational segments (maritime, energy, real estate) results in significant omissions that affect the overall completeness assessment. The score reflects that most core financial and strategic information is present, but critical operational details are lacking.
details.coherence_justification: The candidate summary is fully coherent internally. All statements logically support each other without contradictions. The summary explains the relationship between improved operational metrics (revenue, EBITDA, operating profit) and the decline in net profit through non-recurring effects from prior year consolidation (S4-S5). The structure progresses logically from operational results to financial position and external challenges, with each section building on the previous. There is no unnecessary repetition, and all relationships between figures and explanations are clear and consistent within the document itself. The summary forms a coherent narrative about operational growth offset by one-time prior gains.
